title: Supply, Installation and Commissioning of a Thermal Vacuum Cycling Chamber
description: The School of Physics & Astronomy (Space Park Leicester) has secured funding to procure a Thermal Vacuum (TVAC) System to support environmental testing, qualification, and thermal vacuum cycling of components and equipment developed under the projects run by its Space Projects and Instrumentation group and via commercial agreements with third parties (managed by Space Park Leicester). Thermal vacuum (TVAC) chambers require high-vacuum capability (typically ≤ 1×10−5 hPa), wide-range temperature cycling (often -190 °C to +150°C or higher), and precise thermal control (control surface stability in the range ±0.1 °C/min), usually achieved via liquid nitrogen, shrouds and heating platens. They include contaminant control (e.g. dry pumps), structural reliability to withstand atmospheric pressure, and feedthroughs for power and data to Equipment Under Test (EUT). The System is intended to be installed in an ISO 14644 Class 6 cleanroom at Space Park Leicester.

description: The Department for Education (DfE) is responsible for children’s services including children’s social care in England. title: Omni-Channel Customer Contact Platform
description: The Council requires an omnichannel customer contact centre solution to manage and report on customer interactions across a range of communication channels, including telephone, email and web chat, with the flexibility to extend to SMS and social media where required. The system must support effective enquiry handling, triage and self-service, and provide direct integration with the Council's CRM system, which is used to design and manage back-office workflows. The integration must support real-time, bi-directional data exchange between the contact platform and CRM workflows, including the ability to pass contextual customer data, trigger workflow actions and receive status updates. This will ensure a fully embedded end-to-end service experience, supporting a "right first time" approach, reducing duplication and ensuring enquiries are handled consistently across services. A number of service teams across the Council use the current system. description: This contract was awarded through a direct award under the G-Cloud 14 Framework Agreement (RM1557.14), Lot 2 (Cloud Software). The contract is for the provision, implementation, hosting, maintenance and support of a cloud-based parking suspensions management system for the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC). The solution supports the end-to-end administration of parking suspensions, including customer self-service functionality, workflow management, inspections, enforcement activities, reporting and integration with council systems. The contract also includes associated implementation, training and support services. Contract Start Date: 26 October 2026 Contract End Date (Initial Term): 25 October 2028 Contract End Date (Including Extension Option): 25 October 2029

The scope and potential lot structure will cover a wide range of built environment related professional consultancy services comprising but not restricted to Building Surveying services, Contract Administration, Employers Agent, Quantity Surveying services, and Principal Designer and any other roles that may be required to support the delivery of high quality, on time, on budget works. Support may be required at any project stage from Inception to Post Completion/In Use and may be in relation to Planned Works Programmes, individual works contracts, or any other projects that may arise during the term. The Framework Agreement will be for the provision of construction related professional services by a number of consultants and their supply chains. The Framework will provide national coverage across the United Kingdom (UK). The opportunity is provided for suppliers to identify those areas or regions where they will be able to provide a service.

title: Language Services (Interpreting and Translation) -CPA/SPU/2934P

Language Services (Interpreting and Translation) -Call off Under the National Police Language Services DPS (NW Region ref A1256) - CPA/SPU/2934P.
This call off contract is under Lot 6 Fully Managed Service. A 24/7/365 managed service for the provision of interpreting and language services including
• Face-to-face interpretation;
• Telephone interpreting;
• Video interpretation services;
• Translation and Transcription (including Braille and Easy-read);

title: School and Special Transport Open Framework
description: Bedford Borough Council has a statutory duty to provide free home to school travel for compulsory school-aged children who meet nationally prescribed eligibility criteria and for post-16 students who meet locally determined criteria. To fulfil this duty, the Council commissions transport services from external providers using a range of vehicle types to meet the diverse needs of routes and individual passengers. In addition, the School and Specialist Transport Team arranges transport for a range of Adult and Children's Social Care requirements, including contact sessions, day services, and respite provision. In addition, the School and Specialist Transport Team arranges transport for a range of Adult and Children's Social Care requirements, including contact sessions, day services, and respite provision. To support the efficient and compliant procurement of these services, the Council is establishing a new Open Framework to replace the existing Passenger Transport Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS). The procurement process will be conducted electronically through the ADAM eProcurement System, with approved providers being eligible to participate in future calloff opportunities under the Open Framework.

title: West Northamptonshire Oral Health Improvement Service
description: West Northamptonshire Council has awarded a contract for the delivery of an Oral Health Improvement Service across West Northamptonshire. The service will provide targeted, evidence-based oral health improvement interventions aimed at reducing oral health inequalities and improving oral health outcomes for children, young people, vulnerable adults and older people. Key elements of the service include the delivery of supervised toothbrushing programmes within early years and school settings, oral health training for professionals, support for organisations and settings to promote good oral health practices, partnership working with relevant stakeholders, and the targeted distribution of oral health resources and materials.

title: RRS James Cook MGO Fuel - November 2026
description: Supply of Marine gas oil (MGO), distillate marine fuel to ISO 8217:2024 standard to the RRS James Cook (IMO No. 9338242), Port of Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands. Estimated quantity 380 metric tonnes. Required on the estimated delivery date 04.08.206. All quantities are estimates. The final invoiced quantity will be confirmed by the Bunker Delivery Note for the delivery and by the actual density recorded on the Certificate of Analysis at 15 degrees Celsius. Delivery is by bunker barge or road tank wagon to the vessel at its stated berth or ex pipe within port area. Fuel must comply with ISO 8217:2024/2017 grade DMA. Sulphur content must not exceed 0.10 per cent by mass, as required within the North American Emission Control Area under MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 14. Flash point must be not less than 60 degrees Celsius, in line with SOLAS. Cold flow properties must be suitable for the vessel's operating area and season. Water content, ash, and total sediment must be within the limits set by ISO 8217 for the grade supplied. A single secondary school of approximately 4,315 m² of printed in-scope floor area across three blocks, together with a sports hall building of approximately 1,175 m² delivered under a 2025-26 expansion. A room-by-room schedule of floor surfaces, an out-of-scope list and a sanitary provision schedule are issued with the tender documents. The service. Fully managed: routine cleaning over a 40-week service year, periodic, holiday, deep and non-routine cleaning including high-level work, on-site supervision, labour, equipment, materials, quality assurance and reporting. Washroom consumables are to be priced both as a School-supplied and as a Contractor-supplied option. Points tenderers should note. Timber and sprung timber floors account for 616.6 m², 14.3 per cent of the in-scope area, across five areas including a sports floor and a floor in a food-consumption area. The estate contains 58 WCs, 56 wash basins and 20 showers. There is no site access at weekends or on bank holidays. Kennelling, care and welfare provision for stray dogs. Reunification to owner or if unclaimed, rehomed or humanely disposed of if unsuitable for rehoming. 3. Collection, transportation, temporary accommodation and welfare support for dogs belonging to vulnerable adults where Adult Social Care has a duty of care under the Care Act 2014, and the owner has become hospitalised, incapacitated, detained, or otherwise unable to care for their dog. The research will develop an evidence base to support operational, engineering and standards decisions, including recommendations on how greater conformity in braking performance could be achieved. The work is expected to start in October 2026, with a budget of up to £350,000 excluding VAT, and is anticipated to take less than 12 months.

title: 5085.SH.JN - Advanced Nano-Mechanical Characterisation System with Integrated Fluorescence
description: The University of Sheffield, supported by the Wolfson Light Microscopy Facility (LMF), is seeking the supply, installation and commissioning of a high-throughput nanoindentation platform for the quantitative mechanical characterisation of biological samples and biomaterials. The instrument will provide a centrally managed research resource supporting investigators from across the Faculties of Health, Science and Engineering, together with external academic and industrial collaborators. The system will enable the measurement of mechanical properties across a broad range of biological specimens including single cells, organoids, tissue sections, extracellular matrices, biomaterials and engineered tissues. The University requires an integrated platform capable of combining high-resolution nanoindentation with optical microscopy and environmental control to permit long-term measurements of live biological samples under physiologically relevant conditions. The instrument must also support high-throughput experimentation using standard multi-well plate formats to facilitate large-scale mechanobiology studies and drug screening. Collectively our Members manage more than 90% of UK' social housing stock, with PfH helping them to achieve efficiency savings using a wide range of services including framework agreements, dynamic purchasing systems, spend analyses, strategy reviews, consolidated billing and comprehensive reporting. PfH is a contracting authority under section 2 of the Procurement Act 2023 and a centralised procurement authority under section 1(4) of that Act. Please refer to www.pfh.co.uk for additional information. PfH is administered by Inprova Limited and is headquartered in the North West of England with over 20 years of expertise and experience offering a complete procurement solutions package across outsourcing, technology and consultancy. description: Homes England is currently seeking to appoint a competent Supplier for the provision of landscape maintenance services for 5 Sites within the Northern Arc, Burgess Hill area. Prior to Tendering, Suppliers should ensure that they have the availability and capacity to commence and deliver the Service within a timely manner. Typical planned Services under this contract comprise of but are not exclusively limited to the following: Grass Cutting; Hedge Cutting; Weed Control; and Site Inspection and Cleansing. title: BLC-0177 - Legacy Media Digitisation
description: BlueLight Commercial are looking to implement a Framework for the delivery of Media Digitisation Services. This will include the conversion of legacy media to digital records including meta data for integration with a Digital Evidence Management system. Tender Documentation is scheduled to be published on 11th August and no documentation will be available before this date. The Framework will include 6 lots which are: Lot 1: VHS Media Conversion - In House - With DEMS Integration - This lot is for the provision of software, hardware and training to enable a Customer to convert VHS tapes to digital files and have the files imported via integration with a Digital Evidence Management Solution (DEMS) managed by the Customer. Lot 2: VHS Media Conversion - In House - With DEMS Provided - This lot is for the provision of software, hardware and training to enable a Customer to convert VHS tapes to digital files and have the files available via a Digital Evidence Management Solution (DEMS) provided as part of your solution. Lot 3: VHS Media Conversion - Outsource - With DEMS Integration - This lot is for the provision of conversion services delivered completely by a third party with electron

title: Implementing and Testing a Single Unique Identifier and Data Standards for Children (Local Authority Operational Alpha Pilot)
description: The Department for Education (DfE) is procuring up to four Case Management System (CMS) Suppliers to participate in the Alpha phase of the Single Unique Identifier (SUI) programme and the implementation and testing of data standards for Children. The programme forms part of the Government's commitment to improve Multi-Agency Information Sharing (MAIS) and introduce a SUI for children. It will test the use of the NHS Number as a consistent identifier within Children's Social Care (CSC) systems and the adoption of common data and technical standards through existing local authority CMS platforms. The Alpha phase is intended to generate evidence on technical feasibility, implementation effort, onboarding and assurance requirements, operational impacts, delivery costs and supplier readiness to support future national rollout decisions. Suppliers will work with DfE, NHS England and participating local authorities (LA’s) to integrate with the DfE-hosted "Get an Identifier" service, implement agreed data and technical standards, support testing and live operational activity, and provide evidence and lessons learned to inform future policy, technical, operational and commercial decisions.

title: ES RDE 183 - Legacy Soil Phosphorus Mobilisation Review
description: Environment Agency Self-Service Direct Award. Phosphorus (P) is an essential nutrient for crop growth and food production, with agricultural inputs primarily supplied through inorganic fertilisers and organic manures. However, manures are often applied to meet crop nitrogen (N) requirements, which can result in excess P applications and the gradual accumulation of legacy P in soils. This increases the risk of P losses through runoff, erosion, and leaching, contributing to eutrophication of watercourses. As P is frequently the limiting nutrient in freshwater ecosystems, even small releases can cause detrimental environmental impacts, including algal blooms and oxygen depletion. In England, around 55% of rivers and 75% of lakes fail to meet phosphorus standards under the Water Framework Directive.

A key component of food safety risk assessment is exposure assessment, which estimates the amount of a hazard consumed through the diet. Exposure assessment combines food consumption data with information on the concentrations of substances such as contaminants, food additives or pesticide residues in food to estimate the levels consumers may be exposed to. To conduct UK dietary exposure assessments, the FSA uses consumption data in combination with occurrence data for hazards and other substances in food. This notice is for Lot 6: Suppliers appointed to this lot will provide research, insight and evaluation services that support evidence-led decision-making, programme improvement and impact reporting across the inclusive growth portfolios, programmes or projects. The lot should focus on research, analysis, evaluation and learning rather than strategic consultancy. Typical services may include - Baseline studies, literature searches, evidence reviews, synthesis studies and needs assessments. - Programme logic model and theory of change development. - Impact evaluations, process, outcome and learning reviews including developmental and formative evaluation to support programme improvement. - Quantitative, qualitative and mixed method research study design. - Qualitative research delivery including fieldwork,

title: Supply and Changeout of the Auxiliary Batteries and Battery Trays - Jubilee Line Fleet
description: Transport for London requires the supply, overhaul, refurbishment, changeout and ongoing lifecycle support of the Emergency Standby Battery systems and associated battery trays installed across the London Underground 1996 Tube Stock (96TS) Jubilee Line fleet. The requirement includes replacement battery cells, refurbishment activities, provision and refurbishment of battery trays, associated testing, technical support and ancillary services necessary to maintain system performance and operational availability. The Emergency Standby Battery system is a safety-critical asset which supports emergency lighting, communications systems and train control functionality in the event of loss of normal auxiliary or traction power. The requirement forms part of the first planned lifecycle replacement and refurbishment programme for these assets since introduction of the fleet

description: The Housing Executive currently collects customer payments through a range of channels including payment outlets, online services, telephone, standing order and Direct Debit.
